grandparents_cupboard.reason: Lamb, lentils, root vegetables, cabbage and chicken stock are all plain home-kitchen foods, with no jars, stock pots or packet mixes.

supermarket.reason: Lamb neck fillet, green lentils, celeriac and white cabbage are all stocked by Tesco, and 500g of neck is a reasonable family spend.

basic_kitchen.reason: It needs only a knife, board and a large lidded casserole, and browning and simmering suit a confident beginner.

works.reason: For four, 500g lamb, 200g lentils and 1 litre of stock simmered covered for an hour gives a properly thick stew, and the cabbage cooks in its final 10 minutes.

honest_times.reason: Chopping the lamb and vegetables, peeling the celeriac, browning and a 5-minute soften fit roughly in 25 minutes, and 60 plus 10 minutes of simmering matches the 70 cook minutes.

honest_ingredients.reason: Every listed item, including thyme, bay and lemon, appears in the steps, nothing unlisted is used, and lamb neck fillet matches its id.

seasonal_feel.reason: Half a white cabbage is a substantial part of the pot rather than a garnish, and a hearty lamb and lentil stew suits the turn into early autumn.

plain_voice.reason: Short, clear British English steps with no restaurant language or health preaching.

hearty_healthy.reason: It is a filling meal of lamb, lentils and plenty of vegetables that a family would happily eat again.
